_transcription: PAGE MAP (all 8 render indices accounted for, none unexamined): idx0 = bilingual cover, no question content ('Page 1 of 8', Series ABCD4/3, SET-2, Q.P. Code 65/3/2, code 310 B); idx1 = HINDI General Instructions + Section A Q1-6; idx2 = ENGLISH General Instructions + Section A Q1-6; idx3 = HINDI Section B Q7-10 + Section C header + Q11; idx4 = ENGLISH Section B Q7-10 + Section C header + Q11; idx5 = HINDI Q12, Q13 + Q14 case study; idx6 = ENGLISH Q12, Q13 + Q14 case study; idx7 = BLANK ('Page 8 of 8', carries only a QR code, a stray asterisk, the 310 B code and the footer). ENGLISH PAGES USED: 2, 4, 6 ONLY. The alternating hypothesis HELD, and all three documented failure modes were checked for and did NOT occur: (a) NO English overflow on any odd page - idx1, idx3 and idx5 were each read and are pure Hindi from their first line (idx3 opens on the Hindi Section-B header, idx5 on Hindi Q12), because each language block is laid out as a self-contained mirrored page rather than a continuous flow, so no question straddles a language boundary; (b) there is NO English-only final page (idx7 is blank); (c) there is NO mid-paper parity inversion - Hindi and English occupy exactly 3 pages each. The page pairing is exact: idx1<->idx2, idx3<->idx4, idx5<->idx6 carry the same questions in the two languages. Question numbers run 1 to 14 unbroken with every sub-part present. STRUCTURE CONFIRMED off idx2: 14 questions, 40 marks, 2 hours; Section A Q1-6 @2 = 12, Section B Q7-10 @3 = 12, Section C Q11-14 @4 = 16; Q14 is a case study with 2 sub-parts of 2 marks each. NO MCQs ANYWHERE - every row is subjective, so there are no options and no answer letters; the marking scheme prints a worked 'Sol.' for every question and no 'Ans' letter row anywhere. INTERNAL CHOICE = 4, at Q4, Q7, Q10 and Q11. Instruction (vi) reads only 'There is an internal choice in some questions' and prints NO COUNTS, so the count was NOT taken from the instruction and NOT inferred from the 40-mark sum (which is structurally blind to a missed alternative, since an OR-branch carries no marks of its own). It was established by walking the marking scheme question by question across all 9 content pages: the scheme prints a numbered '(a)'/'(b)' pair separated by a full-width 'OR' row for exactly Q4, Q7, Q10 and Q11, and prints a single un-suffixed block for Q1, Q2, Q3, Q5, Q6, Q8, Q9, Q12, Q13 and Q14. The question paper agrees exactly - 'OR' appears on idx2 (Q4) and idx4 (Q7, Q10, Q11) and nowhere else, with the Hindi mirror printing 'अथवा' at the same four places. MARKING-SCHEME PAGES: ms p00-p01 are the examiner's general instructions (no question content); ms p02-p10 are the scheme proper, running Q1 to Q14 and closing with '* * *'. OVERLAP WITH 65/3/1: 14 of the 19 rows are the same question as a row of the already-transcribed 65/3/1, judged by CONTENT and confirmed on my own page images, then reused byte-for-byte from data/2022-65-3-1.questions.json so they dedup at commit. The mapping (mine -> 65/3/1) is Q1->Q3, Q3->Q5, Q4a->Q6a, Q4b->Q6b, Q5->Q4, Q6->Q1, Q9->Q10, Q10a->Q8a, Q10b->Q8b, Q11a->Q12a, Q11b->Q12b, Q13->Q13, Q14a->Q14a, Q14b->Q14b. All 14 were then re-checked mechanically against the reference file and are byte-identical in stem, context and taxonomy. The 5 genuinely NEW rows are Q2, Q7a, Q7b, Q8 and Q12 - four questions, since Q7 contributes two branches. So the two sets share the SAME 14-question skeleton reshuffled and renumbered, with only Q2, Q7 (both branches), Q8 and Q12 substituted. plan.txt WAS WRONG IN BOTH DIRECTIONS and was not relied on: it claimed 9 shared / 4 new, understating the overlap, and every one of its nine block attributions names the wrong reference question (e.g. it maps my Q2 to 65/3/1 Q4, but my Q2 is the log(dy/dx) = ax+by equation which does not appear in 65/3/1 at all and is one of the new ones, while my Q5 IS 65/3/1 Q4). It also listed Q1 as needing transcription when Q1 is 65/3/1's Q3 verbatim. The marking scheme numbers its blocks exactly as the question paper does (verified block by block), so the mismatch is in plan.txt's block->number attribution, not in a divergent scheme numbering. THE PLANE: Q5 (distance of a point from a plane) and Q13 (line meets plane) are filed on 'The Plane', the subtopic added to the live Three Dimensional Geometry axis on 2026-08-19 for exactly this 2022 Term-2 need. No solutions written: this pipeline authors them later from the marking scheme. TYPOGRAPHY NOTE: as on 65/3/1, the paper is inconsistent about italicising variables - it sets x and lambda italic but y and z upright roman in Q2, Q5, Q9, Q10 and Q12, and prints 'e' upright in x^2 e^x. That is typesetting, not mathematics, and is normalised to ordinary LaTeX italics throughout.

questions.stem: Write the projection of the vector \((\vec{b} + \vec{c})\) on the vector \(\vec{a}\), where \(\vec{a} = 2\hat{i} - 2\hat{j} + \hat{k}\), \(\vec{b} = \hat{i} + 2\hat{j} - 2\hat{k}\) and \(\vec{c} = 2\hat{i} - \hat{j} + 4\hat{k}\).
Find the general solution of the differential equation : \(\log \left( \dfrac{dy}{dx} \right) = ax + by\).
Two cards are drawn successively with replacement from a well shuffled pack of 52 cards. Find the probability distribution of the number of spade cards.

The marking scheme reprints the same stem with the same slip on ms p03, while its own worked solution below it writes 'at least on one die', so the defect is in the question block only. 65/3/1 carries the identical block and the identical slip.
questions.stem: A pair of dice is thrown and the sum of the numbers appearing on the dice is observed to be 7. Find the probability that the number 5 has appeared on atleast one die.

The probability that A hits the target is \(\dfrac{1}{3}\) and the probability that B hits it, is \(\dfrac{2}{5}\). If both try to hit the target independently, find the probability that the target is hit.
If the distance of the point (1, 1, 1) from the plane \(x - y + z + \lambda = 0\) is \(\dfrac{5}{\sqrt{3}}\), find the value(s) of \(\lambda\).

If \(\vec{a}\), \(\vec{b}\), \(\vec{c}\) are three vectors such that \(\vec{a} \cdot \vec{b} = \vec{a} \cdot \vec{c}\) and \(\vec{a} \times \vec{b} = \vec{a} \times \vec{c}\), \(\vec{a} \neq 0\), then show that \(\vec{b} = \vec{c}\).

If \(|\vec{a}| = 3\), \(|\vec{b}| = 5\), \(|\vec{c}| = 4\) and \(\vec{a} + \vec{b} + \vec{c} = \vec{0}\), then find the value of \((\vec{a} \cdot \vec{b} + \vec{b} \cdot \vec{c} + \vec{c} \cdot \vec{a})\).

questions.stem: Show that the lines : \(\dfrac{1 - x}{2} = \dfrac{y - 3}{4} = \dfrac{z}{-1}\) and \(\dfrac{x - 4}{3} = \dfrac{2y - 2}{-4} = z - 1\) are coplanar.
Find the particular solution of the differential equation \(x \dfrac{dy}{dx} - y = x^2 \cdot e^x\), given \(y(1) = 0\).
Find the general solution of the differential equation \(x \dfrac{dy}{dx} = y(\log y - \log x + 1)\).

questions.stem: Using integration, find the area of the region bounded by the curves \(x^2 + y^2 = 4\), \(x = \sqrt{3}\, y\) and \(x\)-axis lying in the first quadrant.

Find the distance of the point (1, -2, 9) from the point of intersection of the line \(\vec{r} = 4\hat{i} + 2\hat{j} + 7\hat{k} + \lambda(3\hat{i} + 4\hat{j} + 2\hat{k})\) and the plane \(\vec{r} \cdot (\hat{i} - \hat{j} + \hat{k}) = 10\).
